children: Dell Technologies
is emerging as one of the clearest hardware beneficiaries of the AI infrastructure boom, with second-quarter results strong enough to trigger major price-target increases from
Morgan Stanley
, Goldman Sachs and Citigroup
. Revenue surged
59% year over year to $47 billion
, while AI-server sales doubled to
$16.4 billion
, reinforcing the view that demand for accelerated computing remains far from exhausted.

Dell sells PCs, traditional servers, storage systems and enterprise infrastructure, but AI servers have rapidly become a major growth engine. The company assembles systems packed with high-end accelerators and networking equipment for hyperscalers, enterprises and other customers building AI capacity.
The scale of the shift is striking. Dell booked
$60.9 billion of AI-server orders
, and Morgan Stanley noted that just four years ago the company generated essentially no AI-related revenue. Dell now expects roughly
$74 billion in AI-server sales
, giving investors direct exposure to the broader data-center buildout beyond chipmakers themselves.

, arguing that continued tight supply and strong execution could keep producing blowout quarters. The bank also pointed to Dell's supply-chain management as a competitive advantage and said traditional server demand remains resilient despite significantly higher prices.

Investors Takeaway
The biggest near-term question is whether supply constraints remain a tailwind rather than becoming a bottleneck. Investors should watch
AI-server backlog, revenue conversion, operating margins and component availability

Continued order growth alongside stronger margins would support the banks' higher targets. But if supply loosens faster than expected, pricing power weakens, or hyperscaler spending slows, the premium being assigned to Dell's AI business could compress quickly. For now, Wall Street sees Dell's hardware position as increasingly central to the AI buildout.

title: Citi Tweaks Dell Stock Price Target For Rest Of 2026
